name: Pregnancy test at 3 weeks
seoDesc: Pregnancy test at 3 weeks: work out your last period from the menstrual cycle length and the urine test date. A free health calculator with the formula,…
summary: Give the Pregnancy test at 3 weeks calculator the menstrual cycle length and the urine test date and it returns your last period. It suits an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Pregnancy test at 3 weeks calculator work?
sections.html:
The Pregnancy test at 3 weeks calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports your last period in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the urine test sensitivity (Natural conception), the embryo's age and the urine test sensitivity (In vitro fertilization)); then you give the urine test date (Natural conception) and the urine test date (In vitro fertilization); then you type in the menstrual cycle length.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A number, expressed in days.
  • A calendar date. Use the picker; the answer is recalculated the moment the date changes, and the count is done date-to-date rather than by subtracting timestamps.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 5 options, such as 20 mIU/mL, 40 mIU/mL and 60 mIU/mL. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 3 options, such as 3 days (cleavage stage), 5 days (blastocyst stage) and 6 days (blastocyst stage). The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A calendar date. Use the picker; the answer is recalculated the moment the date changes, and the count is done date-to-date rather than by subtracting timestamps.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 5 options, such as 20 mIU/mL, 40 mIU/mL and 60 mIU/mL. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.

3 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Pregnancy test at 3 weeks calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Your last period=-menstrual cycle length + urine test sensitivity + urine test date
Ovulation day=menstrual cycle length + your last period − 14
Blood test date=urine test date − 2
IVF transfer day=-embryo's age + urine test sensitivity + urine test date − 12

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Pregnancy test at 3 weeks calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Any time the same 2 figures keep coming back — the menstrual cycle length and the urine test date — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Dates are compared date to date in your own time zone, so a daylight-saving change will not shift the count by a day.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Pregnancy test at 3 weeks calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns your last period, derived from the menstrual cycle length and the urine test date. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Pregnancy test at 3 weeks calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the menstrual cycle length and the urine test date, which is 6 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (3 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Pregnancy test at 3 weeks calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
